outcome.technical: Structural fix per the review. plugins/audit/scripts/_utc_stamp.py: utc_stamp calls argument-less time.gmtime() when epoch is None and time.gmtime(epoch) otherwise (epoch=0 still a moment), so the child sitecustomize that patches gmtime(None) reaches it again. plugins/audit/tests/test__utc_stamp.py: new case us5 patches time.gmtime in-process with a spy and asserts utc_stamp() calls it with no argument and utc_stamp(1700000000) passes the epoch; watched it FAIL before the fix (seen [(1792401906.22,), (1700000000,)], 4/5) and PASS after (5/5). plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py: the frame-inspecting time.time half of the pinned-clock sitecustomize is deleted (back to the HEAD gmtime-only _PINNED_GMTIME, comment and docstring updated); sc4, sc4b (delay 1.2, requires restarted == pin+1) and the al-block budget derived from _harness.stage_timeout() - STAGE_TIMEOUT_MARGIN are kept. Evidence: whole test_drive_phase.py alone ALL PASS 374/374 (exit 0, 2:30 wall); --stage sc-block 6/6 with sc4 and sc4b PASS; test__utc_stamp.py 5/5; ruff check clean on the three files; vermin reports no violations. Red proof for sc4b is the helper run in the submit (HEAD's _utc_stamp.py with time.gmtime(time.time()) plus my test files). Not run: the full tools/sweep-selftests.py and other gate commands (own-tests only); the six-parallel-copies load run was not repeated this attempt (done in attempt 1, 6/6 passed with sc4/sc4b PASS) - the fix is now structural so the pin no longer depends on frame inspection.
outcome.descriptive: The pinned second reaches utc_stamp again because it asks argument-less gmtime(), so sc4 holds its same-second precondition under load without any frame-inspecting patch.
